llm.reply:
Lynch syndrome is represented across NCBI databases by a MedGen condition record, twelve associated genes, and five active or completed clinical trials focused on identification, genetic testing, and patient education [7][19]. The condition is a hereditary cancer predisposition syndrome with published literature spanning genetics, clinical implications, and differentiation from Lynch-like syndrome [18][22][30].

## Causal Genes

The retrieved gene set includes the core mismatch repair genes: mutL homolog 1 (NCBIGene:4292), mutS homolog 2 (NCBIGene:4436), mutS homolog 6 (NCBIGene:2956), PMS1 homolog 1 (NCBIGene:5378), and PMS1 homolog 2, mismatch repair system component (NCBIGene:5395) [10][11][8][13][14]. Additional genes linked to the condition include mutL homolog 3 (NCBIGene:27030), transforming growth factor beta receptor 2 (NCBIGene:7048), epithelial cell adhesion molecule (NCBIGene:4072), cadherin 1 (NCBIGene:999), ribosomal protein S20 (NCBIGene:6224), and neurofibromin 1 (NCBIGene:4763) [6][16][9][17][15][12].

## Condition Record

The condition is documented as Lynch syndrome in MedGen and PubMed [19][18]. Related nosologic entities include Lynch syndrome I (site-specific colonic cancer) and Lynch Syndrome II, as well as the legacy term Colorectal Neoplasms Hereditary Nonpolyposis [20][26][23].

## Clinical Trials

Five trials address Lynch syndrome: a strategy to identify HNPCC patients, a Taiwan-related genetic study, psychosocial aspects of genetic testing, an educational CD-ROM consent intervention, and a registry for women at risk [1][2][3][4][5].

## Current Literature

Recent publications cover Lynch syndrome-associated colorectal cancer, identification approaches, and clinical implications [25][28][30].

Lynch syndrome is represented across NCBI as a hereditary colorectal cancer condition (MedGen: Lynch syndrome) [7] linked to multiple mismatch repair and associated genes, with at least five registered clinical trials and a substantial PubMed literature base.

## Causal and Associated Genes

The core mismatch repair genes identified include mutL homolog 1 (NCBIGene:4292) [10], mutS homolog 2 (NCBIGene:4436) [11], mutS homolog 6 (NCBIGene:2956) [8], PMS1 homolog 1, mismatch repair system component (NCBIGene:5378) [13], PMS1 homolog 2, mismatch repair system component (NCBIGene:5395) [14], and mutL homolog 3 (NCBIGene:27030) [6]. Additional genes associated with the condition include epithelial cell adhesion molecule (NCBIGene:4072) [9], neurofibromin 1 (NCBIGene:4763) [12], ribosomal protein S20 (NCBIGene:6224) [15], transforming growth factor beta receptor 2 (NCBIGene:7048) [16], and cadherin 1 (NCBIGene:999) [17].

## Condition Record

The disease is recorded as Lynch syndrome in the MedGen knowledge base [7][19], with related literature entities including Lynch syndrome I (site-specific colonic cancer) [20], Lynch Syndrome II [26], and Colorectal Neoplasms Hereditary Nonpolyposis [23].

## Clinical Trials

Five registered trials address identification and management: Implementation of a New Strategy to Identify HNPCC Patients [1], Hereditary Nonpolyposis Colorectal Cancer in Taiwan-Related Genetic Study and Clinical Applications [2], Psychosocial Aspects of Genetic Testing for Hereditary Nonpolyposis Colon Cancer [3], Educational CD-ROM Compared With Standard Informed Consent for Patients With Colorectal Cancer or a Family History of Colorectal Cancer [4], and Registry for Women Who Are At Risk Or May Have Lynch Syndrome [5].

## Literature Evidence

PubMed publications include Lynch syndrome [18][21], Differentiating Lynch-like from Lynch syndrome [22][24], Lynch Syndrome-Associated Colorectal Cancer [25][27], Identification of Lynch Syndrome [28][29], and Lynch Syndrome Genetics and Clinical Implications [30].
